lesson.subtitle: Lesson 1 -- The Two Minutes That Introduce You
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Patricia da Silva Granizo Rodrigues | Lesson 1 -- The Two Minutes That Introduce You
lesson.grammar_point: present simple and present continuous for remit and current work

vocab.title: Match each term to its meaning
defs: d
keeping the people you already employ instead of losing them
e
everybody who works for a company, taken together
f
a person or group with an interest in the decision you are making
g
the launch of a new policy or system across the company
h
to have somebody as your direct manager
i
involving people from more than one department
j
to be in charge of work that other people carry out
a
the area of work a person or a department is officially responsible for
b

items.situation: Say what you run at JEM System in one sentence, in the present simple.
tips: I run HR and internal communication for JEM System in Brazil.
One clause. No history, no dates.

items.situation: Now add the second sentence: what is on your desk this quarter?
tips: At the moment I am rolling out a new performance cycle.
The continuous is what makes it sound current.

items.situation: Somebody answers: So you are running HR temporarily? What went wrong in your sentence?
tips: You used the continuous for something permanent.
I run HR, not I am running HR.

items.situation: How many people does JEM System employ in Brazil? Use the word from today.
tips: Our headcount in Brazil is just under two hundred.

items.situation: Greg asks what else sits with you besides HR. Answer in one sentence.
tips: Internal communication sits inside my remit as well.
Remit is the word an American director would use.

items.situation: Ask Greg the same question back, the way an American would.
tips: And what are you working on at the moment?
Not what is your work. What are you working ON.

listenings.text: Patricia, it is Greg. I know it is late for you, so I will keep this short. Starting in September we are moving the people review to a monthly call instead of a quarterly one, and I would like you on it every time. Twenty minutes, no deck, just the numbers and what you are working on. Nobody here expects a presentation. What we do expect is that you own the number and you can say what is behind it. If retention moved, say why it moved. If a rollout slipped, say what slipped and what you are doing about it. One more thing. You do not have to wait for me to ask. The people who do well on that call are the ones who bring the problem before somebody else finds it. Talk on Monday.

Let me tell you how I describe my job, because it took me years to get it short. I run people operations for the eastern region. That is the sentence that never changes. Then I add one line about what is on my desk this quarter, and this quarter it is a benefits change that affects about nine hundred people. Two sentences, and that is the whole introduction. What I used to do was tell people my entire history, and I could see them waiting for me to stop. Americans are not being rude when they cut in. They are trying to find the hook, the thing they can ask you about. So give them the hook early. Say what you run, say what you are working on, and then ask them the same question back.
